summary: Epilogue JSON object lost when SSE stream passes through H2->H1 conversion on customer LB (fan-out)
description: Customer reports that the final JSON object in an array produced by an SSE conversational stream is missing on their consumer when requests flow through an on-prem F5 load balancer that performs HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 conversion and fan-out to multiple backend worker connections. The truncated object causes the customer's downstream parser to error and the UI to show an incomplete bulleted list at the end of responses.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer has Redwood Private deployed behind F5 LB configured to accept gRPC/h2 on the front and proxy to backends over h1.
2) Open an SSE stream for a multi-paragraph answer containing a final JSON array (e.g., choices array with multiple objects).
3) Trigger a mid-stream connection fan-out (LB opens parallel backend connections for the same session token) via health probe or stickiness change.
4) Observe consumer-side parse failure or missing terminal object in the array.
logs:
Customer-provided capture: last-sse-event: 'data: {"choices":[{"text":"..."},{"text":"Partial end', heartbeat: 'data: 
' followed immediately by 'data: {"session_heartbeat":true}
'
Redwood ingress logs: connection_id=abc123 h2->h1 conversion path detected, backend_conn_reset=1 at 2026-03-13T14:22:34Z
SDK (node) reports JSON.parse error: 'Unexpected end of JSON input' at client line 213
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: LB is coalescing or splitting SSE 'data:' frames when mapping between HTTP/2 and HTTP/1.1 which can slice JSON object boundaries mid-object.
- Reproduced locally by setting up an h2->h1 proxy with aggressive write coalescing: JSON array's last object can be split across TCP packets; some proxies remove interstitial 0-length CRLFs used as delimiters.
- Noticed difference vs hosted environment: Redwood hosted ingress preserves explicit event boundaries by flushing per-event. Private on-prem path relies on underlying LB to preserve chunk boundaries; our runtime didn't add an extra sentinel for private deployments.
- Checked SDK behavior: node and python SDKs buffer stream by newline; partial-object that lacks closing '}]' produced parse errors instead of waiting for final event.
- Correlated with customer's LB configuration: 'HTTP/2 to HTTP/1.1 conversion - response coalescing = enabled' and 'parallel backend reuse = on' which results in mid-stream backend swap.
- Related internal ticket INT-4120 tracks robust SSE framing for noisy middleboxes.
- Quick experiment: when we force per-event flush and add an explicit framing marker ("__RW_EVENT_END__") the customer's parser no longer fails even when the LB splits packets.
resolution:
Workarounds: 1) Customer changed F5 setting to disable aggressive response coalescing and set stickiness to preserve single backend per session; validated on 2026-03-13 17:10 UTC and customer reported immediate improvement. 2) Short-term server-side mitigation: enable per-event flush sentinel for Private deployments via config flag 'sse.strict_event_flush=true' (rolled out to customer's private control plane 2026-03-14).
Permanent fix and next steps: 1) Backport runtime patch to always append an event boundary sentinel for SSE streams in private deployments where upstream indicates H2->H1 conversion; PR #2145 opened and awaiting security review. 2) Update node/python SDKs to tolerate partial-object buffering by waiting for event terminator tokens and to treat sentinel as delimiter. 3) Add runbook entry and automated probe to detect H2->H1 coalescing in customer environments.
Follow-ups: schedule config-change webinar for private customers and roll code fix to Dedicated by 2026-03-21.
